plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It aims for steady, low-drawdown performance by eliminating leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration. Expect lower volatility but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Buy RGTI at 4% as a strong scanner setup to add quality tech exposure.

balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5%/month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality scanner setup. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential with a reasonable cash buffer.

plan: Add to SOXL and SPAL, bringing each to 6%, to increase leveraged ETF exposure.
Buy RGTI at 6% as a strong scanner setup, leaning into high-scoring opportunities.
Add to CRWD, bringing it to 15%, and SMH, bringing it to 13%, to press what is working.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month, aiming for stretch growth by using leverage and concentrating in high-scoring setups. This approach significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this mode can lose a lot fast; strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Add to QQQI, bringing it to 40%, to prioritize income and covered-call exposure.

income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, prioritizing low drawdown and reliable income. It focuses on income/covered-call ETFs and broad index exposure, cutting high-beta names. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is cash-like income, not a savings account.
